title: Lemon Blueberry Tart
description: Lemon condensed-milk filling with a blueberry swirl on shortbread.
beforeYouStart: Make the blueberry sauce first. Once the crust is in the oven, everything moves fast.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) while the sauce cooks.
Check the condensed milk: it must be full-fat sweetened, and a full 14 oz can. Evaporated, fat-free or a short can leaves the filling runny.
Don't use a springform pan; the crust leaks.

items.item: Lemon slices, blueberries, leftover sauce, whipped cream

items.do: Stir the cornstarch into the lemon juice with a fork until dissolved; set aside.
Warm the blueberries and sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3 min, stirring now and then and mashing the berries against the pan to break them down.

Stir in the slurry and cook 2 min more, then take off the heat and leave at room temperature until the filling goes in. It makes 1/2 to 2/3 cup; about half goes in the tart and the rest is for serving.
Melt the butter for the crust. Zest one lemon, then juice about 2 to make 6 Tbsp for the filling.
In a medium bowl, stir together the melted butter, sugar, vanilla and salt. Add the flour and mix until fully combined.
items.cue: Thick and a little greasy, as it should be

items.do: Press firmly and evenly into an ungreased 9-inch tart pan, across the bottom and up the sides. It looks like too little but it stretches. The base of a measuring cup helps, though it can stick.
Poke a few fork holes across the warm crust, not all the way through, so the filling has something to grip. Leave the oven on.
Whisk the condensed milk, lemon juice, zest and egg yolk until smooth. Pour into the still-warm crust.

Stir the sauce to loosen it, since it thickens as it sits; give it 5 to 10 sec in the microwave if needed (warm is fine). Spoon about half over the filling and swirl with a toothpick or knife, then shimmy the pan back and forth two or three times to settle it.
Bake at 350°F (175°C). Err toward underbaking; it keeps firming in the fridge, and overbaked filling turns rubbery.
items.cue: Center stops jiggling when you tap the pan; top still a little tacky

items.do: Cool completely on a rack, then refrigerate uncovered. Cover it if chilling longer than 2 hr, up to 1 day.
items.wait: At least 2 hr in the fridge

items.do: Remove the pan sides, slice, and serve with the reserved sauce and any garnishes.
uses: Lemon slices, blueberries, leftover sauce, whipped cream

items: Leftovers keep tightly covered in the fridge up to 1 week.
The whole tart can be baked and chilled a day ahead. It also freezes up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge.
The sauce and filling can be made ahead and refrigerated (rewarm the sauce to loosen it), but don't prebake the crust. The filling needs a warm crust to stick.
Pan: a 9-inch pie dish works with the same bake times but slices less cleanly. A graham crust doesn't work; it collapses under this filling.
Smooth sauce: strain it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove skins and lumps.
Lime: swap lime juice and zest for the lemon. The swirl is optional.
Strawberry: 1 cup chopped fresh or frozen strawberries in place of the blueberries.
Raspberry or blackberry: 1 cup berries plus 1 extra tsp sugar in the sauce (3 tsp total). Strain out the seeds.

Mini tarts: divide the crust among about 10 mini tart pans, pressing it into the bottoms only. Bake 8 min on a sheet pan and skip the fork holes. Fill the warm crusts, dot and swirl with sauce, and bake 9 to 10 min until the centers set. Cool, then chill at least 1 hr.
Orange isn't recommended (too sweet without the tang). Grapefruit is untested.
